entities.text:
High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Nagpur Bench At Nagpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant has preferred the present appeal challenging the judgment and order dated 25.07.2025, passed by the learned Extra Joint District Judge and Additional Sessions Judge (Special Judge, POCSO Court), Nagpur, in Special Criminal (Child) Case No. 693/2021.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge (Special Judge, POCSO Court), Nagpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the said judgment, the applicant stands convicted for the offence punishable under Section 366 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years and to pay a fine of Rs. 3,000/-, and in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months.

2. The learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was tried for offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(3), and 376(2)(j) of the IPC, 2 9--appa- 658-25.odt as well as under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, "the POCSO Act").

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Upon due appreciation of the evidence led by the prosecution, the learned trial Court acquitted the applicant of the charge under Section 4 of the POCSO Act but convicted him under Section 366 IPC.
3.
It is contended that the finding of conviction recorded by the trial Court is unsustainable and contrary to the evidence on record.

The learned counsel submits that the victim, in her deposition,
did not name the applicant while narrating the incident, and even the medical evidence does not connect the applicant to the alleged crime.
It is, therefore, urged that the applicant has a strong prima facie case and fair chances of succeeding in the appeal.

It is further submitted that the Vijay S/O Pritam Rathod vs State Of Maharashtra Thr Its Station ... on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110642437/
1 applicant was on bail during the trial and has not misused the liberty granted to him.

entities.text: Vijay S/O Pritam Rathod vs State Of Maharashtra Thr Its Station
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State opposes the application, contending that the conviction is based on cogent and reliable evidence.
He submits that there are certain discrepancies regarding the name of the accused, which the applicant is now seeking to exploit.
Considering the gravity of the offence, he submits that no case is made out for suspension of sentence.
It is further urged that if the applicant is released, there is a likelihood of tampering with the prosecution witnesses.
I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record and proceedings.
Upon a prima facie perusal of the testimony of the victim, it appears that the specific role of the present applicant in the incident is not clearly established.
Moreover, the applicant was on bail during the trial and there is nothing on record to show that he misused the liberty so granted.

6. In view of the above and considering the arguable points raised in the appeal, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.
7. Accordingly, the application is allowed.

The substantive sentence imposed by the learned Extra Joint District Judge and Additional Sessions Judge (Special Judge, POCSO Court), Nagpur, in Special Criminal (Child) Case No. 693/2021, vide judgment and order dated 25.07.2025, is hereby suspended, subject to the following terms and conditions:
I. The applicant/appellant shall be released on bail on furnishing a PR bond of Rs.
20,000/- with one solvent surety in the like amount before the trial court.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge (Special Judge, POCSO Court), Nagpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: II. The applicant shall report before the concerned trial Court on the first day of every calendar month until further orders.

III. The applicant shall furnish his current 4 9--appa- 658-25.odt residential address and mobile number to the concerned Sessions Court and shall inform the Court forthwith of any change in address or contact number.
The application stands disposed of accordingly.
Heard.
ADMIT.
Issue notice to the respondent.
